Published online:
    September 9, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Japan, Global (with specific reference to US, Switzerland, Mexico, New Zealand)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    The article examines the yen carry trade — borrowing low-rate yen to invest in higher-yielding assets — amid a surge in the yen to a seven-month high. It traces the trade's origins to Abenomics in 2013, its peak build-up through 2022-2023, and the shock July 2024 BOJ rate hike that triggered a violent unwind. Currently, annualised returns on dollar-yen carry trades have compressed to 2.5-3.5% (down from 5-6% in 2024), and some investors are rotating to Swiss franc funding. With the BOJ widely expected to hike again at its imminent meeting, markets are watching for another potential unwind, though current yen moves are described as orderly and equity markets appear composed.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: NO — the primary focus is on the BOJ and the yen carry trade; US rates appear as a contextual input, not the main message.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 10 (low relevance — US rate hikes are referenced historically as a driver of carry trade build-up, not as a current forward-looking theme)
Probability of increase: 15%

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 20 (implied stable-to-declining US rates are part of the backdrop, narrowing the rate differential with Japan, but not explicitly discussed)
Probability of holding: 35%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 30 (the compression in carry trade returns from 5-6% to 2.5-3.5% implies the US-Japan rate differential is narrowing, consistent with a US rate cut narrative, though not stated explicitly)
Probability of decrease: 50%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: -35 (Moderately dovish — the narrowing carry trade premium and compressed dollar-yen yield differential point toward a market pricing in lower US rates relative to prior years; the BOJ tightening cycle is the dominant narrative, which by contrast implies a relative dovish lean on the US side)
